question: Compute direct-port phase spectra on the unordered E plus T2 shear current and compare signed incidence.

objects.definition: Copy a current coordinate to its two incident face flags
objects.domain: mean-zero ordinary R^6, E plus T2
objects.metric_measure: Euclidean edge, symmetric blocks on flags

assumptions: Single regular cell, unit Euclidean current metric and source-only preparation.
Flag record metric block diagonal by face, identical symmetric diagonal/off-diagonal coefficients in every face.
Signed and unsigned carriers typed independently.

technique_plan.technique: exact Gram spectra and signed incidence comparison
technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: test whether equivariant locality forces degenerate nonzero rates

integer_fraction_receipt.raw_count_expression: four faces × three flags = six edges × two flags

clock_receipt.update_rule: closed skew exchange with declared adjoint

dynamics_readout.state_space: unordered mean-zero edge currents plus auxiliary flag coordinates
dynamics_readout.projection_and_kernel: unsigned coherent face sum kills E; signed joint module has no E

target_exposure.search_domain_and_budget: declared face-local invariant metric family and incidence checks

calculation_steps: Count flag diagonal and cross incidences
Diagonalize ordinary adjacency on opposite-pair modes
Check signed cut and cycle Grams separately

result.exact_expression: squared rates (2(u-v),2u); unit flag rates sqrt(2) and sqrt(2)
result.scope: Independent Euclidean flags give (2,2) squared rates. Equivariant face cross terms split them. Coherent face sums give (0,2). The signed joint incidence port has squared rate 4 but its module has no E.

counterexamples_and_failures: Positive S4-equivariant cross metric splits rates
limitations: No native selection of independent flag ports or metric
Stage-two depletion and deficit allocation open
next_discriminant: Derive a native flag metric and observed port separation before using the common-phase latch; otherwise test sector-resolved receipts.
